title: Rate limiter lets bursts through, then locks users out forever
summary: Our API rate limiter allows one request too many, and once a user hits the limit they stay blocked even after the window passes. Memory also keeps growing.
brief: src/rateLimiter.js implements a sliding-window rate limiter: createLimiter({ limit, windowMs, now }) returns { allow(key), remaining(key) }. A key may make at most `limit` requests within any `windowMs` window. Requests older than windowMs must stop counting (a request made exactly windowMs ago no longer counts) and must be pruned from memory. Keys are independent. Keep the exported API unchanged, including the `_size(key)` debugging helper.

visibleNames: allows exactly `limit` requests in a window
allows again after the window passes
hiddenNames: a request exactly windowMs old no longer counts
remaining() reflects the sliding window and never goes negative
